options.text: Splitting CSS files into smaller chunks
Dividing JavaScript bundle into multiple chunks that load on demand

questions.explanation: Code splitting divides the JS bundle into smaller pieces that are loaded only when needed, reducing the initial load.

questions.prompt: Which asset type benefits most from lazy loading?
questions.explanation: Lazy loading defers loading images that are not initially visible, improving perceived performance.

questions.prompt: Core Web Vitals metric that measures perceived loading speed?
questions.explanation: LCP indicates the time until the largest content element becomes visible, reflecting perceived loading speed.

questions.prompt: Which method is commonly used to implement code splitting in React?
questions.explanation: React.lazy loads a component asynchronously, enabling code splitting.

questions.prompt: Which technique directly reduces First Contentful Paint?
questions.explanation: Server-side rendering pre-renders content, allowing the browser to display it faster, thus reducing FCP.

questions.prompt: How can you programmatically measure LCP using the PerformanceObserver API?

options.text: Measure network timing for image loads

questions.explanation: The PerformanceObserver can observe 'largest-contentful-paint' entries to capture LCP.
